maria: Heads-up: saw a perf regression in latest canary when enabling FP8 kernels + CUTLASS INT8 fallback. TL;DR: ~15% slower on long-chat workloads. Anyone else?

perf-bot: nightly-run: model-chat_long: p50 latency +15%, tokens/sec -12% vs baseline (sm80, fp16 baseline). See /perf/reports/1719876543 :mag:

alex: I pushed a quick bisect: regression introduced in last week's build when we set -DUSE_FAST_MATH=OFF for correctness tests. That changed math approximations and broke some Triton fused FP8 kernels. Also our CUTLASS path selection logic started preferring FP8 for small seqs which should be faster, but calibration quant params are off so there's extra layout/conversion overhead.

jin: Found that KV cache alignment is causing small batches to be padded to 128 in our batching heuristic; when combined with FP8 kernels that assume contiguous KV strides, we do extra copies -> big overhead. Repro: seq_len=2048, batch=2, kv_stride ends up misaligned.

sam: Interesting. Can you paste the perf diff/profile?

jin: ```
perf top (sample):
python inference main: memcpy + kernel_launch overhead spikes when using fp8_triton_kernel
Kernel timings (avg):
  triton_fp8_self_attn: 1.8ms -> 2.4ms
  cutlass_int8_gemm: 0.9ms -> 0.92ms
  cpu memcpy: 0.3ms -> 1.1ms
```

alex: So two root causes: (1) CPU memcpy from layout conversions due to KV cache alignment + batching heuristic; (2) reduced kernel efficiency when fast-math off. Short-term fixes: re-enable fast-math for release builds; add arch detection to prefer CUTLASS INT8 on sm80+ and fallback to Triton FP8 only for sm90+ where FP8 kernels are tuned. Also add a runtime toggle --prefer-cutlass for int8 so we can A/B quickly.

maria: Proposal: implement a runtime kernel-selection policy that considers model seq-length distribution and batch size. Heuristics: 
- if batch >= 8 or batch * seq >= 8192 -> prefer cutlass_int8 (better GEMM throughput, fewer copies)
- if seq > 4096 -> prefer fp16/float fallback (memory bandwidth dominated)
- if kv_cache.enabled and kv_stride % 64 != 0 -> force layout-preserving path to avoid copies
Also add a calibration job during onboarding to generate per-layer quant params (avoid quality regressions).

jin: I'll draft a PR for kernel-selection + an env var REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=cutlass|triton|fp16. Also adding a microbench in CI to catch regressions: chat_short, chat_long, batch_inference on sm80 and sm90.

maria: :thumbsup: Also log selected kernel and reason in request trace (redwood.trace.kernel) so we can correlate perf and quality.

perf-bot: Added perf regression alert to the thread. Next run scheduled for tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

sam: One more note: calibration vs latency tradeoff. Per-layer calibration (50k tokens) adds onboarding time; suggest sampling-based calibration + iterative background refinement where we start conservative and refine quant params after N live tokens.

maria: Thanks, team. Keep PRs small. Jin -- assign reviewers alex + sam. I'll open a follow-up ticket for KV-cache layout refactor and drop a perf-run checklist in the ticket.
